subject: applying a different function to each column of a data frame

messages.author: 8954cb0a46bd963a
messages.subject: applying a different function to each column of a data frame
parts:
Hi D-RUG folks.

Does anyone know of a function for the following purpose?  I would like to apply a list of functions to the columns of my data frame so that the first function in the list would be applied to the first column, the second function would be applied to the second column, the third function would be applied to the third column, etc.  Is there a way to do this without using a loop?

Bonnie

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: applying a different function to each column of a data frame
parts:
Hi, Bonnie.  I don't know that  there's any harm in using a loop, although using a loop does seem to lose you some style points in the R community.

One approach to avoiding the explicit use of a loop would be to name the columns of your data frame and name your functions with the same names.  Then you could iterate over the names, as per the appended code, which applies the function "sum" to the first column of a data frame and the function "mean" to the second column.  (Note that the formatting may have suffered in the transition to email.)

-- Mike

myFns <- list(odds=sum, evens=mean)
myDF <- data.frame(
      cbind(
          odds=c(1, 3, 5, 7),
          evens=c(2, 4, 6, 8)
      )
   )

myDF

result <- lapply(names(myFns), function(nextName) {
      myFns[[nextName]](myDF[[nextName]])
})

unlist(result)
